minutes.headline: Assessors voted to ratify Rina Sweezy as interim principal assessor immediately, over loud public objection.
minutes.summary: The Board of Assessors heard a long run of angry public comment about the FY23 tax assessment error and the proposed interim assessor. The town manager asked the board to ratify her appointment, and the board debated waiting two weeks. A motion to ratify immediately was moved and seconded and passed by voice vote. The board then heard about the vision revaluation and certification timeline, discussed its work plan and policies, and moved toward executive session.

public_comment.topic: Read a colleague's statement thanking staff for abatements and asking what procedural changes, reviews and training will prevent a repeat, and how the intern/interim assessor was chosen.
Questioned the hiring process and the interim candidate, who he said had defended the prior assessor's work. Said his own land card was still wrong and his new bill was higher despite an abatement.
Opposed the interim assessor over her record in Groton and other towns, and said the abatement process was stressful on a limited income.
Said there is public outrage, asked why Zoom was off, and put forward a vote of no confidence in the interim principal assessor.
Asked why public comment comes before the agenda, why not outsource assessing to a firm, and why questions go unanswered.
Asked who makes the final hiring decision, the board or the town manager, and feared the same lack of management.
Opposed hiring the interim assessor, urged an outside contractor, and raised benefit and retirement costs.
A resident said afternoon meetings do not work for working people and asked for a more accessible time.

votes.motion: Ratify the immediate appointment of Rina Sweezy as interim assessor (an amendment to wait two weeks was floated but not adopted).
Move into executive session, with a roll call requested.

budget_items.what_was_said: Delays in new construction and split lots could mean lost revenue. This was a critical task for the next couple of weeks.

what_happened.line: The Board of Assessors voted by voice to ratify Rina Sweezy as interim principal assessor immediately; an amendment to wait two weeks was floated but not adopted.
The chair reordered the agenda to take the interim assessor's ratification first, ahead of other business.
Residents spoke against the interim appointment and asked for an outside firm, and one put forward a vote of no confidence.
The town manager said she will ask the state Department of Revenue to extend the revaluation certification deadline to January.
The board asked the town manager to report on her communications with the Department of Revenue and her recommended procedures; the Vision contract is still to be put together.

why_it_matters: The FY23 assessment error led to abatements and refunds the board's own members described as a cash-flow strain on the town, so who runs the assessor's office bears on tax bills and town finances.
The revaluation is done by an outside firm under a contract not yet written, and its certification date depends on a state extension, which affects when residents see updated property values.
watch_next: The town manager's report to the board on her Department of Revenue communications and recommended procedures.
Whether the Department of Revenue grants the extension of the revaluation certification to January, and when the Vision contract is signed.
